Subject: Finlytics discovery recap + next steps (SDK auth, routing, embed/reranker)

Alex â€” thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a reliable repro for the 5xx behavior you saw: 

Summary from today's call:
- Primary use case: real-time search assistant over Finlytics docs + customer data.
- Planned flow: client -> Redwood SDK (embed endpoint for indexing + reranker for search-time re-rank) -> structured output/tool-calling for metadata extraction.
- Auth: you will use API keys for now, later move to VPC private endpoints.
- Routing: plan to route high-priority live queries to Dedicated pool; fallback to hosted model variant.

Action items / next steps:
1) Finlytics: send a minimal repro (curl + sample payload + timestamps) when you hit the 5xxs. Prefer logs and the exact request body.
2) Redwood: Marissa and Neha will attempt local repro and advise on timeout/client tuning.
3) Camila: I'll coordinate and keep track on the HubSpot deal (FTLY-2026-089).

For reproducibility please include: a) exact request payload, b) response headers (x-request-id, x-ray-id if present), and c) approximate time windows. If possible attach a small .zip with logs.

I'll follow up internally after we reproduce. Thanks â€”

Camila Reyes

camila@redwood.ai

From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Finlytics discovery recap + next steps (SDK auth, routing, embed/reranker)

Thanks Camila â€” attaching the repro files per your checklist. We see 5xx errors only when sending combined embed + reranker requests from our backend. Quick summary:
- Time windows: 2026-11-12 07:40 - 08:15 UTC (multiple occurrences)
- Pattern: first request in a short burst returns 200; subsequent requests (burst of 6-8 within ~10s) yield 500 Internal Server Error.
- Example x-request-id: rwd-req-9a7b2c
- Sample response snippet:
  HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
  Content-Type: application/json
  {"error": "internal_server_error", "message": "unexpected server error"}

Attachments included: repro_payload.json, finlytics_repro_logs.txt (server + client logs), repro_steps.zip (small repro harness).

Notes: we are using the JS SDK v0.10.1 with default client timeout (10s) and sending requests to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate with a composite payload (embeddings + reranker call in a single logical flow). Let us know if you need additional headers or logs.

Appreciate the quick help â€”
Alex
Principal Infra Engineer
Finlytics
alex.taylor@finlytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@finlytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:15:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Finlytics discovery recap + next steps (SDK auth, routing, embed/reranker)

Alex â€” thanks for the artifacts, this is helpful. I pulled the repro and ran a few local tests against our staging endpoint. Initial observations and troubleshooting steps: 

1) Burst behavior looks like request queueing + a backend transient where the model worker throws a KV cache resync error before recovering. We're seeing 429s/rate-limit-like backpressure in some internal traces, but your client logs show 500s which indicates an uncaught server exception in the reranker path.

2) Quick mitigations to try on your side (non-breaking):
   - Increase client timeout from 10s -> 20s to allow backend fallback/rehydration. Example (JS SDK):
     const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, timeout: 20000 });
   - Add an explicit routing hint header to pin to a lower-latency model variant while we investigate: X-Redwood-Model-Variant: rwd-embed-rerank-v1
   - Reduce burst concurrency: add a small jitter/backoff when sending multi-request bursts (50-200ms).

3) Request payload issue: your repro_payload.json includes a combined embed+rerank pipeline that sometimes exceeds our payload size thresholds and causes a serialization error in the reranker microservice. I attached a minimal patched payload (see `repro_payload.json` line notes) that splits embedding and rerank into two logical calls â€” this should be a stable workaround while we patch the server-side deserialization.

4) Repro request for Redwood SRE: please include one example curl with the failing headers and the x-request-id/time window; we will tail logs and link traces.

Marissa (cc Neha) will take the server-side trace once you confirm a failing curl and time. We should be able to identify the exact stack trace and apply a fix or safe-guard within 24-48 hours.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Platform Support Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2026 08:03:27 -0800
Subject: Re: Finlytics discovery recap + next steps (SDK auth, routing, embed/reranker)

Marissa â€” quick update after applying your recommended mitigations:
- Increased timeout to 20s and added X-Redwood-Model-Variant header.
- Reduced concurrency with a 100ms jitter.

Result: after ~2 hours of load testing, we saw zero 500s. I still attached the earlier logs where we saw the failures (finlytics_repro_logs.txt). Please proceed to pull traces for the time window 2026-11-12T07:40:00Z - 2026-11-12T08:15:00Z and x-request-id rwd-req-9a7b2c.

Also attaching repro_steps.zip containing a small Node harness to reproduce locally if you want to run the same burst profile.

If you confirm a server-side fix is planned, we will remove the workaround and validate against production traffic. Thanks for the rapid help.

â€”Alex

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>

Subject: Finlytics - next steps and timeline

Alex â€” great to hear the mitigations removed the 500s in your load tests. Next steps from our side: 
- Marissa: prioritize a hardening PR to the reranker deserializer and add a defensive payload-size check (target ETA: 24 hours).
- Neha: follow up on routing pinning and Dedicated pool configuration for FTLY-2026-089 (ETA: vendor config by EOD Friday).
- Camila: I'll keep the HubSpot deal updated and coordinate an engineering verification session once the server-side fix is deployed.

Alex â€” when the fix is live we'll request that Finlytics runs a short smoke test (5â201310 minute burst) and confirm there are no regressions. Thanks for the detailed repro and the quick turnaround on the client-side mitigations.

Best,
